content:
maya: rolling NF4 -> FP4 canary into prod at 03:12 UTC, noticed a 18-25% throughput drop for long-context jobs and memory spikes on rtx-pools.
kevin: saw elevated OOMs in canary logs, any tracebacks?
maya: short logs pasted below, looks like KV cache resizing thrash + lots of generic kernels picked by runtime.
maya: ```
[2026-03-12T03:14:01Z] tokens/sec down 22% on /generate (model:xl-nf4)
[2026-03-12T03:14:02Z] mem.used jumped 14GB -> 46GB on pod-rt-23
[2026-03-12T03:14:02Z] kernel_selector: chose generic_matmul_v2 for layers 12-24
[2026-03-12T03:14:03Z] kv_cache: realloc pages=3 -> 12, page_faults=7
```
lina: interesting — kernel_selector choosing generic_matmul_v2 is the smoking gun. That kernel is slower for packed 4-bit layout. Should prefer packed_dot_q4 kernels.
dario: did profiling show less vectorized/warp-level kernels? perf-bot: attached flamegraph for 03:10-03:20 canary window -> /artifacts/flame_1749812345.svg
kevin: quick check: are we hitting a calibration path that toggles kernel preferences? We changed quant calibration to prefer minimal fp-loss and that might flip block sizes.
maya: yes, ML team changed calibration table last week — NF4 bias table now favors per-tensor scales leading to smaller GEMM tiles.
lina: two orthogonal issues: (1) kernel selection heuristic uses heur_score = occupancy_est * memory_efficiency - and calibration altered memory_efficiency -> picks lower-throughput kernel; (2) KV cache op pattern: realloc on growing seq length not amortized, causing paging.
dario: repro locally with long prompt (16k) and batch=1 shows similar memory pattern. Quick diff I ran:
```
# repro
./run_infer --model ./xl-nf4 --seq_len 16k --batch 1 --quant nf4 --kernel-selection=auto
# profile
nvprof --profile-from-start off --metrics gld_throughput,gst_throughput ./run_infer ...
```
kevin: can we force packed_dot_q4 kernel to validate perf? If yes, we can hotpatch selector to prefer it for nf4 until we fix heuristic.
maya: I tested forcing `--kernel-selection=packed_dot_q4` in canary: tokens/sec +28% vs auto but memory still slightly high (~+4GB) due to KV realloc pattern.
kevin: ok hotpatch plan: (A) runtime flag to bias toward packed_dot_q4 for nf4/short-batched requests, (B) defensive KV alloc guard to preallocate based on expected max_seq for route, (C) revert calibration table change if calibration-induced kernel choices persist.
lina: also consider batching heuristic: continuous batching windows are too eager for long-context clients so they create many small batches that kill kernel occupancy. Increase continuous_batch_window_ms from 8 -> 25 for long-seq routes as a canary.
dario: we should quantify quality difference if we revert calibration. ML-team: can we run evals on our cal-set with forced packed_dot_q4 and with previous calibration? Need delta on perplexity / bot safety checks.
maya: ML-team ran quick eval: delta negligible (<0.2% pPL) on our long-context eval set, but some edge cases had subtle tokenization drift. I'll attach eval ids later.
kevin: ops-bot, roll canary changes? ops-bot: @maya canary rollout queued: runtime.hotfix/1749812345 -> canary pool (5 pods) at 03:45 UTC :spinner:
maya: monitoring dashboards to watch: route/tokens_per_sec, route/p50_latency, pod/mem_used, pod/oom_count, selector/chosen_kernel_distribution.
lina: also add a new trace tag for calibration_version on model load so we can correlate kernel picks with calibration tables.
dario: I'll open infra/issue and assign to eng-runtime + eng-ml: include perf logs, flamegraph, and sample request IDs. Suggest naming: infra#6142.
maya: temporary mitigation: enable kernel bias flag and preallocate kv to max_expected_seq. If that stabilizes, we can roll to remaining production traffic and schedule full fix.
kevin: rollback criteria: if tokens/sec stays <90% baseline for 10m or OOMs >5 in 15m, rollback to previous quant config.
maya: 👍 starting hotfix canary in 5m. I'll post updates.
kevin: thanks — please ping #incidents if it spikes.
maya: update 03:52 UTC: canary hotfix showed tokens/sec back to baseline and OOMs dropped to 0 across canary pods. Further load test on staging with batch=8 shows stable perf.
lina: great, but keep the calibration revert discussion — we need root cause: calibration -> changed quant scale granularity -> kernel scoring -> bad kernel picked. That's a subtle coupling.
dario: longer term: add perf-tests into calibration CI that assert chosen kernel profiles for representative seq lengths.
maya: filing follow-ups: infra#6142 (hotfix/monitor), ml#342 (calibration rollback + eval), perf#829 (selector heuristics + CI).
maya: end of thread update 04:20 UTC: hotfix promoted to 30% traffic, metrics holding.
